newsitem.title: UK: Sears marked up after restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Sears marked up after restructuring.

text.p: Shares in British retailer Sears Plc were marked higher in pre-market trading on Tuesday after it announced a group restructuring and profits in line with forecasts, dealers said on Tuesday.
Sears' shares were up three pence, or 3.87 percent, to 80.5p by 0710 GMT in volume of 35,000.

Sears announced the demerger of its profitable Selfridges department store, said it had conditionally agreed the sale of its Freemans mail order arm to Littlewoods for 367.5 million pounds ($600 million) and said it intended to return the net proceeds to shareholders.
Also, Sears' beleaguered chief executive Liam Strong is to leave the group.
Analysts had forecast pre-tax profits in a 75-80 million stg range. Sears' 88.9 million stg pre-tax pre-exceptional included a 7.9 million stg pension credit. Profit before tax was 68.1 million stg.
Sears said overall like-for-like sales were up 5.3 percent in the first 11 weeks of the current year.
It said it would return about 370 million stg to shareholders.
